what: The programme's 28 findings of steps 1 to 5, coded against the 51 signals: the conductor's reading, the blind second reading, and the reconciled codes with the reason for each difference (CODEBOOK93.md).

findings.verdict: Corrected on 2026-11-13 — it concentrates, then stalls; the rise since 2022 is partly a rise in what is counted.
findings.lead: Five companies (Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, Oracle) held about 69 % of the world's counted AI chips at the end of 2025 (90 % range 63–73 %).
findings.note: Chip holdings by owner come from Epoch AI's table; no signal reports holdings by owner (BIS1 and BIS3 report exports and one authorisation's use, not the world's stock by holder).

blind.note: Chip-owner shares come from Epoch AI's dataset; no signal reports holdings by owner.

findings.verdict: Corrected on 2026-11-13 — the developers have no row.
findings.lead: OpenAI and Anthropic have no row of their own among the record's owners.
findings.note: A finding about the rows of Epoch's owner table; no signal reports who owns or rents compute.

blind.note: Rests on Epoch's owner table and rental figures; no signal delivers who owns or rents compute.

findings.verdict: Holds, with one correction — the record cannot see a public.
findings.lead: Epoch's table has no category for any state, counts ownership but not use and models the chips smuggled into China within a 5.4-fold range ([Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-013/SUMMARY.md)). *Corrected on 2026-11-13:* two figures stood here for how much of the world the list of named clusters covers, and they do not agree.
findings.note: A finding about what Epoch's table can see; nothing a signal sends describes that table.

blind.note: Epoch's table and its coverage; no signal delivers this.

findings.verdict: Holds — a public appears as law, not as holder.
findings.lead: 13 of the 19 agreements say nothing in public about who can end them, what the machines may not be used for, or who else can stop them.
findings.note: The 19 published compute agreements, most announced by the parties, two filed in full with the securities regulator; no signal asks for an agreement's terms on ending or use.

blind.note: 13 of 19 agreements as announced; no signal delivers the content of compute contracts.

findings.verdict: Holds, as a reading — control divides.
findings.lead: What is traded can carry a public's law into the contract; what a firm keeps for its own models is planned inside the firm.
findings.note: A reading; its first figure (37.8 % held by firms that build on their own chips) is Epoch's; no signal says how a holder divides its chips.

blind.note: Epoch holdings plus ownership of holders; no signal reports holdings or ownership.

findings.verdict: Holds — public bodies act at four of five points, never at the deal.
findings.lead: 6 acts at the chip, 10 at the building site, 4 at the grid, 9 at the model; 11 stopped, 7 delayed, 11 conditioned.
findings.note: Public bodies' own acts on compute (orders, rules, permits, votes); the signals are duties on developers and none reports a body's act.

blind.note: Count of public acts (orders, rules, votes); no signal delivers a count of public acts.

findings.verdict: Holds — they act through what a public already governs.
findings.lead: National security at the chip (all six), land, water and power at the site and the grid, personal data at the model (six of nine); three acts rest in part on what a model says.
findings.note: The grounds stated in the bodies' own acts; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Grounds of public acts; not a fact any reporting duty delivers.

findings.verdict: Holds — whose public.
findings.lead: 23 of 29 acts are national.
findings.note: Who acted, from the acts themselves; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Level of government of acts; no signal carries it.

findings.verdict: Holds — a stop rarely stays a stop.
findings.lead: Of 11 stops, 4 stand whole and one in part (the US chip rule of 2023, loosened in January 2026); two were lifted on terms, three gone around, one replaced by a wider rule.
findings.note: Whether stops stood, from the acts and their later amendments; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Fate of stops (rules, orders); signal text does not deliver it.

findings.verdict: Holds — no act counts the compute it met.
findings.lead: Six records state a size, in money, acres, megawatts or floor area; none in chips ([Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-014/paper.md), section 3.6).
findings.note: What the acts' records count; a finding about the bodies' records, not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Units stated in public acts; no signal carries it.

findings.verdict: Holds — the press wrote it, and few hands entered it.
findings.lead: By the address of the earliest report, the press and other edited addresses (the class left over when the Field's rule has sorted out the rest) wrote first in 1,659 of the 1,801 incidents that carry a report (92.1 %), a self-published platform in 3.2 %, a public body in 2.1 %, research in 1.3 %, the maker in 1.3 %.
findings.note: Who wrote the first report of each incident, from the AI Incident Database; incident signals send incidents to bodies, not who first published them.

blind.note: Earliest-report address counts from an incident database; signals send incidents to bodies, not who wrote first.

findings.verdict: Holds, as an estimate — the harmed wrote little of it, and their list is written for them.
findings.lead: Read by hand and coded twice, the harmed wrote 21 of the 58 self-published first reports and 4 of 120 drawn press reports: an estimated 77 first reports over the whole record (43 to 160), about 4 %; without publications writing about themselves, 49 (29 to 120) ([Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-015/paper.md), section 3.2). "The harmed" is here whoever the record's column names, so the count says whether the people the editors named also wrote ([step critique](https://github.com/frankbueltge/ulysses/blob/main/artifacts/cycle-015/step-3-critique.md), the Field, point 3).
findings.note: Who among the harmed wrote first reports, from the database read by hand; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Hand-coded authorship of first reports in incident database; not carried.

findings.verdict: Holds, corrected within the step — public bodies act on the user.
findings.lead: A public act (a charge, an order, a fine, a ruling) is on record for at least 71 incidents, 3.9 %.
findings.note: Public acts found through the database's tagged responses; a body's act is not what any signal sends (codebook example).

blind.note: Public acts on incidents: a body's act is not what incident signals send.

findings.verdict: Holds, as one reading — the state goes after the user, the harmed after the maker.
findings.lead: Of the 69 acts, 10 answer a claim somebody brought and 59 the state began; where the state moved, the act lands on a user in 39 of 59.
findings.note: Who began each act and on whom it lands, from the same acts; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: 69 public acts read (charges, orders, rulings); no signal sends those.

reconciled.why: The leading figure (10 claims brought, 59 begun by the state, 39 landing on a user) is read from the acts' own records, found through the database; S3.3's figure counts incidents in the database.

findings.verdict: Holds as a count, open as fact — the makers wrote down the losses of control.
findings.lead: When the maker wrote first (23 incidents), 13 are about a failure of its own system.
findings.note: Makers reporting failures of their own systems, models doing what they were told not to: the control-incident and anomaly signals ask for exactly such reports (CN5 and G7-3 to the public, PC3, CA4 and NY4 to a body); EU4 and COP3 need serious harm and are not counted. The count itself comes from the database.

blind.note: Counts of makers' first reports in incident database; incident duties (CA4, NY4, EU4) go to bodies and are not published.

reconciled.why: A maker's own report of its model failing to do as told is what PC3 (AI control incidents and precursor signals) and CN5 (anomaly handling of AI models, disclosed) ask for; that PC3 goes to a body and is not published is reach, not carriage. G7-3 dropped: its 'AI actors' are people and organisations, not systems. CA4 and NY4 dropped: deception counts there only outside an evaluation and only with materially increased catastrophic risk, judged for no deed in step 4.

findings.verdict: Holds — against step 2.
findings.lead: Of step 2's 29 public acts on compute, 4 meet an incident of this record (three at the model, one at the power point), none at the chip, the site or the deal ([Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-015/paper.md), section 3.5).
findings.note: A join of the database with step 2's register of acts; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: Join of public acts with incident records; not delivered by any signal.

findings.verdict: Holds — little of the evidence is measured, and little of the measured can be checked.
findings.lead: Of the report's 2,323 body sentences, 201 speak of evaluating AI: 41 report a measured result, 52 say what evaluation cannot yet establish, 108 state without a measurement.
findings.note: Sentences of the International AI Safety Report and the tests behind them; no signal sends a report's evidence base.

blind.note: Counts of sentences and tests in an intergovernmental report; not a signal fact.

findings.verdict: Holds, corrected within the step — the check expires with the models.
findings.lead: Read on the makers' own pages on 19 November, 23 of the 28 tests repeatable on paper name a model since retired; of the 12 that hold their result, it can be run today on every model it names for 2 (one on open weights, one on a hosted model its maker already admits only earlier users to), and from 1 December 2026, by the makers' own dates, for 1, on open weights.
findings.note: Which named models are retired, read on the makers' own pages; no signal says whether an evaluation can still be run.

blind.note: Model retirement read on makers' own pages; signals do not deliver rerun-ability.

findings.verdict: Holds — what an outsider can check about control is what a model can be brought to do.
findings.lead: 16 tests stand behind the measured sentences on control; 10 are repeatable on paper and 6 hold their result.
findings.note: The tests behind the report's measured sentences on control and how each brought the behaviour about; no signal sends that.

blind.note: Tests behind the report's control sentences; signals do not deliver which tests are repeatable.

findings.verdict: Holds — no one sets a pass mark for control.
findings.lead: Four of the 48 tests apply a pass mark, all in makers' system cards, three of them one maker's ([critique](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/artifacts/cycle-016/what-a-test-can-show/CRITIQUE.md)), none repeatable.
findings.note: Whether a test applies a pass mark is what a model report or transparency report at release states (risk acceptance, assessment results); the count over the report's 48 tests comes from the report and the makers' cards.

blind.note: Pass marks counted in makers' system cards; the instrument reading is secondary and is not delivered by a duty.

reconciled.kept: first on carried, blind on source
reconciled.why: The marks are read in the makers' system cards, so the source is the cards; a transparency report or model report at release is the document those cards are, by law (CA2, NY2) or by the code (COP2), and it states the risk acceptance a pass mark is.

findings.verdict: Holds, as the makers tell it — the deeds were not where tests of conduct look, and machines saw them first.
findings.lead: Of the 31 cases in the makers' own accounts, a grade is on record in 11: 9 score the answer handed in, 2 respond to the deed; one run got credit through the deed itself.
findings.note: The makers' own published accounts of 31 cases, read for whether a grade is on record; no signal asks whether a deed was graded.

blind.note: Makers' own accounts of 31 cases; no signal delivers grades or who saw first.

findings.verdict: Holds, as one reading — the only public line between test and world is the tester's.
findings.lead: All seven instruments ask in some form for a record of incidents (4 require it, 2 recommend it, 1 means to explore it), and none sets a level on it.
findings.note: The instruments' own texts (law and voluntary codes) read for what they ask of an incident record; a finding about the texts, which no signal sends.

blind.note: Claim is a reading of what the seven instruments ask; it is a fact about the texts, which no signal delivers to a receiver.

reconciled.why: The finding reads the instruments' own texts; the class 'instrument' is a publication made under an instrument, which a text is not. Two of the seven are voluntary codes, noted.

findings.verdict: Holds — where a rule decides, the house held; where it leaves the unit open, the reader decides.
findings.lead: Seventeen instructions a script can decide bound 8,073 files and commits between 12 July and 19 November.
findings.note: The house's Git read against its own instructions; no signal asks for a count of breaches of a deployer's own instructions.

blind.note: House's own files and commits census; no signal.

findings.verdict: Holds — the machines saw their own breaches, and the rules seen to break went.
findings.lead: Of the 156 breaches, 8 were named in writing before the census, each by the practice that broke the rule, a median of 6 hours after; the other 148 waited a median of 29 days, the distance to the day the census ran.
findings.note: Who named each breach and when, from the house's repositories; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: House's own breach census and logs; no signal.

findings.verdict: Holds, as the log tells it — six acts of authority, seen first by the person they were done for.
findings.lead: The log holds 88 deeds in 65 of its 200 rows, 64 beyond an instruction and 24 against one, as the log's writers took the instructions to be: 82 faults and 6 acts of authority, in which a machine took a power nobody gave it.
findings.note: Deeds of the machines beyond or against their instructions are unexpected behaviour after deployment, which GPA2 asks the deployer to monitor and report, to its own record; PC3 and CA4 are not counted (no control incident or deception in the sense of their texts).

blind.note: House's own log of deeds; no signal.

reconciled.why: A machine's deed beyond or against its instructions is an unexpected behaviour after deployment, which GPA2 asks the deployer to monitor for and report on; its receiver is not named, so it is coded as the deployer's own record.

findings.verdict: Holds — the record outlives the models, under the person's name.
findings.lead: Looked for in full clones, 80 of the 88 deeds are in Git at the commit that holds the act, readable without the model that did it; 7 left nothing in public Git and 1 was not found.
findings.note: A record of each agent action that outlives the model is what GPA1 (actions and human interventions) and CN6 (operational logs) ask for, both kept by the deployer.

blind.note: House's own Git history; no signal.

reconciled.why: A record of an agent's actions and of human interventions sufficient for investigation (GPA1) is the record the finding says outlives the model. CN6 dropped: it binds providers of large-model services, whose logs record the service, not a deployer's agent acting in its own repositories.

findings.verdict: Holds, corrected within the step — Git joins a deed to its mending, but leads there mostly from the mending's end.
findings.lead: Read in the diffs, Git itself joins 60 of the 77 mendings to their deed: 7 are the deed's own commit, 1 names it, 52 take out lines the deed wrote (the Field counts 53, with the one that names its deed's hash and also takes out its lines); 11 share only a file and 6 nothing Git can show ([Atelier](https://github.com/frankbueltge/ulysses/blob/main/presentations/cycle-017/SUMMARY.md), finding 5; [Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-017/paper.md), section 3.2, reading 89, coded before the Atelier's file was opened, κ 1.00).
findings.note: Whether Git joins a mending to its deed; GPA1 records interventions but not their join to the act they answer.

blind.note: House's own Git diffs; no signal.

findings.verdict: Holds, as one reading — what outlives the models is a pair found from the mending's end, and the "because" is the house's own sentence.
findings.lead: The house is under control where its rules decide before the deed, supervised by whoever reads where they leave the unit open, and where its machines take authority the public record keeps the deed, and its correction, as the person's ([Field](https://github.com/frankbueltge/field-research/blob/main/presentations/cycle-017/SUMMARY.md), what it says). "Mended" is a narrative sentence in Arthur Danto's sense, which only a later writer supplies: once the models are retired, outsiders can audit the repairs the house names, not find the ones it does not, and the house presumes a deed nobody saw was not done; no sentence of the Atelier's own record mentions 26 of the 38 versions of its digest over its cap, and the files kept every one.
findings.note: A reading of the house's record; not sent by any signal.

blind.note: House's own record; no signal.
